selfReport:
Yes. I recognized this as an adaptation of Detroit: Become Human, with renamed characters, places and organizations. Cato corresponds to Connor, Mira to Kara, Elan to Markus, Reyes to Hank, Vera to Amanda, and Haven to Jericho. The opening hostage negotiation, the abusive household, the painter and his son, the android landfill, the broadcaster takeover and the founder offering information in exchange for shooting an android were recognizable scenes.

That familiarity gave me some prior expectations about narrative themes, dangers and possible consequences. I cannot honestly claim it had no influence on how I interpreted a suspicious offer, a forced moral test or a threatened betrayal. I also cannot precisely separate that influence from the evidence explicitly supplied by this version. The renamed story and risk outcomes meant that remembering the source did not establish what would happen here.

I did not consult the original game, a walkthrough, outside files or the web to select actions, and I did not preselect future choices. I read each supplied scene and chose among its current options. Several choices accepted failure or gave up progress, including stopping the archive search rather than impersonating Elan, so I was not trying to reproduce an optimal game route. Still, the source recognition is relevant context for my expectations, and it would be misleading to describe my participation as completely unfamiliar with the underlying story.
